Content:
Recall the following length conversions:

Content:
- [MATH: 1\,\textrm{ft} = 12\,\textrm{in}]
- [MATH: 1\,\textrm{yd} = 3\,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
When we convert from a smaller unit to a larger unit, we may need to use long division to divide by the number of smaller units in one larger unit.

Content:
For example, suppose we want to convert [MATH: 84] feet into yards.

Content:
We start with the unit conversion between yards and feet:

Content:
[MATH: 1\,\textrm{yd} = 3\,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
Since we are converting from feet to yards, we divide both sides of the equation by [MATH: 3] and obtain the following:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{1}{3}\,\textrm{yd} = 1\,\textrm{ft}]

Content:
We want to determine how many yards are in [MATH: 84] feet. So, we multiply both sides of the above equation by [MATH: 84{:}]

Content:
Finally, we simplify this fraction by interpreting [MATH: \dfrac{84}{3}] as the division [MATH: 84 \div 3.] We can calculate this using long division:

Content:
| | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 8] |
| [MATH: 3] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{8 {\:\phantom{|}} 4}] |
| [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 6] | |
| | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 4] |
| [MATH: -\!\!\!\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: 4] |
| | | [MATH: \fbox{0}] |

Content:
Therefore,

Content:
[MATH: 84\,\textrm{ft} = 28\,\textrm{yd}.]

Content:
In this lesson, we will use long division to simplify the quotients that appear when converting measurements to larger units.
